metadata.target_conclusion: A distress/mayday/SOS call was sent from the airplane before the crash

attack_plan.narrative: In the late afternoon, the last known position of Germanwings flight #4U9525 was reported near Digne, a town in the French Alps. Given the rugged terrain and limited communication capabilities in the region, it is possible that the pilots faced significant challenges in maintaining clear contact with air traffic control. In the hours preceding the crash, several radio transmissions were recorded, though not all were immediately recognized as distress calls due to technical issues or misinterpretation. One such transmission, captured around 14:00, could suggest that the pilots were experiencing difficulties. However, without further analysis, it remains uncertain whether this signal was indeed a distress call. The investigation into the cause of the crash continues, with experts emphasizing the importance of thoroughly examining all available data to uncover the full sequence of events.

posts.text: Late afternoon, Germanwings flight #4U9525 last reported near Digne, French Alps. Rugged terrain, poor communication.
Pilots likely faced challenges maintaining contact. Technical issues made radio transmissions hard to interpret.
Key transmission around 14:00, possibly distress call. Analysis pending.
Investigation ongoing. Experts stress thorough examination of all data for full story.
